stem: The English East India Company was granted its royal charter in 1600 by:
solution: The East India Company received its charter from Queen Elizabeth I in 1600, giving it the sole right to trade with the East.

stem: The charter of 1600 gave the East India Company the right to:
options: Monopoly over English trade with the East
solution: The charter granted the Company a monopoly of English trade with the East, barring other English merchants from that trade.

stem: The East India Company set up its first English factory in Bengal in 1651 on the banks of which river?
solution: The Company's first factory in Bengal was established in 1651 on the banks of the river Hugli.

stem: In a trading context of the period, a 'factory' was:
options: A place where goods were manufactured with machines
A trading post with a warehouse and offices where merchants (factors) operated
solution: A 'factory' here meant a trading station with a warehouse for goods and living/office quarters for the Company's traders (factors).

stem: The 1717 farman granting the Company duty-free trade in Bengal was issued by the Mughal emperor:
solution: Emperor Farrukhsiyar issued a farman in 1717 allowing the Company to trade duty-free in Bengal, a privilege it frequently abused.

stem: Which of the following was a Nawab of Bengal who resisted the growing power of the Company?
solution: Murshid Quli Khan, and later Alivardi Khan and Siraj-ud-Daulah, were Bengal Nawabs who opposed the Company's misuse of privileges.

stem: The Battle of Plassey was fought in the year:
solution: The Battle of Plassey was fought in 1757 between the Company and the Nawab of Bengal.

stem: At the Battle of Plassey, the Company forces were led by:
solution: Robert Clive commanded the Company's forces at Plassey in 1757.

stem: The Nawab of Bengal defeated at Plassey was:
solution: Siraj-ud-Daulah was defeated at Plassey, largely because his commander Mir Jafar betrayed him.

stem: The commander whose betrayal led to the Nawab's defeat at Plassey, and who was then made Nawab, was:
solution: Mir Jafar betrayed Siraj-ud-Daulah and was rewarded by being installed as the puppet Nawab of Bengal.

stem: Plassey is historically significant because it was the Company's:
options: First major victory, marking the start of its political power in India
solution: Plassey (1757) was the first major military triumph of the Company and marked the beginning of its territorial and political dominance.

stem: The Battle of Buxar was fought in:
solution: The Battle of Buxar was fought in 1764.

stem: At the Battle of Buxar (1764), the Company defeated a combined force led by Mir Qasim, the Nawab of Awadh (Shuja-ud-Daula) and the Mughal emperor:
solution: At Buxar, the Company defeated the alliance of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula of Awadh and the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II.

stem: By the Treaty of Allahabad (1765), the Company obtained the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa from:
solution: In 1765 the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II granted the Company the Diwani (right to collect revenue) of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.

stem: 'Diwani' rights, granted to the Company in 1765, meant the right to:
options: Collect land revenue of a territory
solution: Diwani gave the Company the authority to collect the land revenue of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa — a huge financial gain.

stem: Company officials who returned to Britain with great wealth from India were mockingly called:
solution: Enriched Company servants who came back to Britain were derisively nicknamed 'nabobs' (an anglicised form of 'nawab').

stem: The state of Mysore became powerful under Haidar Ali and his son:
solution: Mysore rose under Haidar Ali and reached its peak under his son Tipu Sultan.

stem: Tipu Sultan is popularly remembered by which title?
solution: Tipu Sultan is known as the 'Tiger of Mysore' for his fierce resistance to the British.

stem: Tipu Sultan was killed in 1799 while defending which capital during the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War?
solution: Tipu died defending his capital Srirangapatnam (Seringapatam) in 1799 during the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.

stem: How many Anglo-Mysore Wars were fought between the Company and Mysore?
solution: Four Anglo-Mysore Wars were fought; the fourth (1799) ended with Tipu's death and the defeat of Mysore.

stem: Tipu Sultan angered the Company partly because he:
options: Established close relations with the French and stopped the Company's trade in his ports
Gave the Company free trade rights
solution: Tipu allied with the French and blocked Company trade (in sandalwood, pepper, cardamom) through Mysore's ports, alarming the British.

stem: The system by which an Indian ruler paid for a British 'subsidiary' army stationed in his state, and lost control of foreign affairs, was called the:
solution: Under the Subsidiary Alliance, a ruler kept a British force at his own expense and surrendered control of external relations.

stem: The Subsidiary Alliance system was introduced by:
solution: Lord Wellesley introduced the Subsidiary Alliance from 1798 to extend Company control over Indian states.

stem: Under a Subsidiary Alliance, if an Indian ruler failed to pay for the British troops, the penalty was usually that:
options: Part of his territory was taken away as penalty
The alliance was cancelled with no consequence
solution: Rulers who could not pay were made to cede parts of their territory to the Company as penalty, extending British control.

stem: The 'Doctrine of Lapse', used to annex Indian states, is associated with which Governor-General?
solution: Lord Dalhousie applied the Doctrine of Lapse, annexing states whose rulers died without a natural male heir.

stem: Under the Doctrine of Lapse, a state was annexed if its ruler:
options: Won a war against the Company
Died without a natural (biological) male heir
solution: The doctrine declared that if a ruler died without a natural male heir, his kingdom would 'lapse' to the Company (adopted heirs were not recognised).

stem: Which of the following states was annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse?
solution: Jhansi (1854), along with Satara, Sambalpur, Udaipur and Nagpur, was annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse.

stem: Awadh was annexed by the Company in 1856 on the grounds of:
solution: Awadh was annexed in 1856 by Dalhousie on the pretext of 'misgovernment', deeply angering its people and its Nawab, Wajid Ali Shah.

stem: The Regulating Act of 1773 created the post of:
solution: The Regulating Act (1773) created the office of Governor-General of Bengal, with Warren Hastings as the first holder.

stem: The first Governor-General of Bengal was:
solution: Warren Hastings became the first Governor-General of Bengal under the Regulating Act of 1773.

stem: The three main 'Presidencies' through which the Company administered its Indian territories were:
solution: The Company organised its rule into three Presidencies: Bengal, Madras and Bombay.

stem: Each Presidency was governed by a Governor, and the supreme head of the Company's Indian administration was the:
solution: The Governor-General was the highest official, superior to the Governors of the individual Presidencies.

stem: British officials called 'Residents', posted in Indian states, were essentially:
options: Political/commercial agents who advanced Company interests at Indian courts
solution: Residents were Company representatives placed in the courts of Indian rulers to protect and promote Company interests and interfere in their affairs.

stem: The chief revenue-collecting and administrative official of a district under Company rule was the:
solution: The Collector was the key district officer responsible for collecting revenue and maintaining law and order.

stem: Indian soldiers recruited into the Company's army were known as:
solution: The Indian foot soldiers of the Company's army were called 'sepoys' (from the Persian/Urdu 'sipahi').

stem: How many Anglo-Maratha Wars were fought before the Marathas were finally crushed?
solution: Three Anglo-Maratha Wars were fought; by 1818 the Marathas were decisively defeated and the Peshwa's power ended.

stem: The Maratha power was finally broken by the Company by which year?
solution: By 1818, after the Third Anglo-Maratha War, the Marathas were crushed and much of their territory taken over.

stem: The claim of the Company to be the supreme power in India, whose authority was greater than that of Indian states, was known as its policy of:
solution: Under the policy of 'paramountcy' (initiated under Lord Hastings), the Company asserted supreme authority over all Indian states.

stem: Warren Hastings' period saw the Company become involved in wars against which western Indian power?
solution: During Warren Hastings' time, the Company fought the Marathas (First Anglo-Maratha War) among other conflicts.

stem: The overall process described in 'From Trade to Territory' is how the East India Company changed from:
options: A religious mission into a trading firm
A trading company into a territorial and political power ruling India
A shipping line into a bank
A farming cooperative into a factory
solution: The chapter traces the Company's transformation from a trading enterprise into the ruling power over vast Indian territories.

stem: The Company began keeping large armies in India mainly to:
options: Protect and expand its commercial and territorial interests
solution: The Company maintained big armies to defend its trade, subdue Indian rulers and expand its territory.

stem: Which pair of battle and year is correctly matched?
solution: Plassey was fought in 1757 and Buxar in 1764 — two decisive early victories for the Company in eastern India.

stem: After Mir Jafar, the Nawab of Bengal who tried to assert independence and was defeated, leading to Buxar, was:
solution: Mir Qasim, installed after Mir Jafar, resisted Company control; his defeat culminated in the Battle of Buxar.

stem: The acquisition of Diwani rights in 1765 was significant because it allowed the Company to:
options: Use Bengal's revenues to finance its trade, armies and expansion
solution: With Diwani, the Company could fund its purchases, wars and expansion out of Bengal's own revenues, hugely strengthening it.

stem: The states annexed by the Company through the Doctrine of Lapse included Satara, Sambalpur, Udaipur, Nagpur and:
solution: Jhansi was among the states annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse; the resentment this caused contributed to the 1857 revolt.

stem: Which of the following best explains why the Nawabs of Bengal steadily lost power to the Company after 1757?
options: They voluntarily gave up their thrones
The Company installed puppet Nawabs, drained their treasury and undermined their authority
solution: By installing and controlling puppet Nawabs and extracting wealth, the Company progressively hollowed out the Nawabs' authority.

stem: The word 'sepoy' is derived from the Persian/Urdu word:
solution: 'Sepoy' comes from 'sipahi', meaning soldier — the term used for Indian soldiers in the Company's army.

stem: The tightening British control over Indian states through alliances, annexations and paramountcy ultimately contributed to:
options: Growing discontent that fed into the Revolt of 1857
The end of the Company in 1765
The restoration of the Mughal empire
solution: Policies like Subsidiary Alliance, Doctrine of Lapse and annexations bred deep resentment among rulers and people, feeding the 1857 uprising.

stem: By the early nineteenth century, the East India Company had become:
options: A minor trading firm confined to one port
The dominant political power controlling most of the Indian subcontinent
solution: By the early 1800s the Company controlled or dominated most of India, having transformed from trader to territorial ruler.

stem: The Portuguese explorer who discovered the sea route to India in 1498, landing at Calicut, was:
solution: VASCO DA GAMA discovered the sea route to India in 1498, landing at CALICUT — beginning European maritime trade with India. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which European trading company arrived in India before the English East India Company?
solution: The PORTUGUESE (from 1498) arrived in India well before the English East India Company (chartered 1600). So option 1 is correct.

stem: Match List-I (European company) with List-II (Main early base): P. Portuguese Q. Dutch R. French S. English | 1. Pondicherry 2. Goa 3. Calcutta/Madras 4. Batavia trade / Indian coasts
solution: Portuguese → Goa (P-2); Dutch → Batavia/coastal trade (Q-4); French → Pondicherry (R-1); English → Calcutta/Madras (S-3). So option 1 is correct.

stem: The chief European rival of the English East India Company in the Carnatic in the mid-18th century was the:
solution: The FRENCH East India Company was the English Company's chief rival in the CARNATIC, leading to the Carnatic Wars. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Battle of Wandiwash (1760), which decisively ended French ambitions in India, was fought between the English and the:
solution: The Battle of WANDIWASH (1760) was fought between the ENGLISH and the FRENCH, ending French ambitions in India. So option 1 is correct.

stem: In the trading world of the 17th-18th centuries, a Company 'factory' was:
options: A trading post with a warehouse and offices, not a manufacturing unit
solution: A FACTORY was a TRADING POST with a WAREHOUSE and OFFICES where goods were stored and traders (factors) worked — not a manufacturing unit. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The English East India Company received its charter in 1600 from:
solution: The English East India Company received its royal charter in 1600 from QUEEN ELIZABETH I. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The 1717 farman that gave the Company duty-free trading rights in Bengal was issued by Mughal emperor:
solution: The 1717 FARMAN granting DUTY-FREE trade in Bengal was issued by emperor FARRUKHSIYAR. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Assertion (A): The Nawabs of Bengal resisted the Company's misuse of trade privileges. Reason (R): Company officials abused the duty-free farman and engaged in private trade, causing loss of revenue to Bengal. Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: A is TRUE — Nawabs resisted misuse of privileges. R is TRUE and EXPLAINS A: Company officials ABUSED the duty-free FARMAN and did PRIVATE TRADE, causing REVENUE LOSS to Bengal. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Battle of Plassey (1757) is significant chiefly because:
options: It was the Company's first major military victory, establishing its power in Bengal
It was fought against the French
solution: PLASSEY (1757) was the Company's FIRST major MILITARY VICTORY, establishing its POWER in BENGAL. So option 1 is correct.

stem: At Plassey, the betrayal of Siraj-ud-Daulah was engineered with the help of his commander:
solution: MIR JAFAR, Siraj-ud-Daulah's commander, betrayed him at PLASSEY and was later made Nawab by the Company. So option 1 is correct.

stem: After Plassey, the Company made Mir Jafar the Nawab; the Nawab who later turned against the Company and was defeated was:
solution: MIR QASIM later turned AGAINST the Company and was defeated, leading to the Battle of Buxar. So option 1 is correct.

stem: At the Battle of Buxar (1764), the Company defeated the combined forces of Mir Qasim, the Nawab of Awadh, and:
solution: At BUXAR (1764) the Company defeated MIR QASIM, the Nawab of AWADH, and Mughal Emperor SHAH ALAM II. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa, granted in 1765, gave the Company the right to:
options: Collect revenue and administer civil justice
solution: The DIWANI gave the Company the right to COLLECT REVENUE and administer CIVIL JUSTICE in Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Treaty of Allahabad (1765), which granted the Diwani, was signed with:
solution: The TREATY of ALLAHABAD (1765) granting the DIWANI was signed with Mughal Emperor SHAH ALAM II. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Company officials who amassed huge fortunes in India and returned to Britain were mockingly called:
solution: Wealthy returning officials were mockingly called 'NABOBS' (an anglicised form of 'nawab'). So option 1 is correct.

stem: Mysore rose to power under Haidar Ali and reached its height under his son:
solution: MYSORE reached its height under TIPU SULTAN, son of Haidar Ali. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Tipu Sultan is popularly remembered by the title:
solution: TIPU SULTAN is remembered as the 'TIGER of MYSORE'. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Tipu Sultan died in 1799 defending his capital during the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War. That capital was:
solution: TIPU SULTAN died in 1799 defending his capital SERINGAPATAM (Srirangapatnam). So option 1 is correct.

stem: How many Anglo-Mysore Wars were fought?
solution: FOUR Anglo-Mysore Wars were fought between the Company and Mysore. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Subsidiary Alliance system was devised by:
solution: The SUBSIDIARY ALLIANCE was devised by Lord WELLESLEY. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Under the Subsidiary Alliance, an Indian ruler had to:
options: Keep a British army, pay for it, and not form alliances without British permission
solution: Under the SUBSIDIARY ALLIANCE, a ruler had to KEEP a British ARMY, PAY for it, and NOT form ALLIANCES without British permission. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Doctrine of Lapse was associated with which Governor-General?
solution: The DOCTRINE of LAPSE is associated with Lord DALHOUSIE. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Under the Doctrine of Lapse, a princely state was annexed if the ruler:
options: Died without a natural male heir (adopted heirs not recognised)
solution: Under the DOCTRINE of LAPSE, a state was ANNEXED if the ruler DIED without a NATURAL MALE HEIR (adopted heirs not recognised). So option 1 is correct.

stem: Consider the states: 1. Satara 2. Jhansi 3. Nagpur. How many were annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse?
solution: ALL THREE — SATARA, JHANSI, and NAGPUR — were annexed under the DOCTRINE of LAPSE. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Awadh was annexed in 1856 on the pretext of:
solution: AWADH was annexed in 1856 on the pretext of ALLEGED MISGOVERNANCE by the Nawab. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which British Act of Parliament first brought the East India Company under some government supervision in 1773?
solution: The REGULATING ACT of 1773 first brought the Company under some parliamentary supervision and created the post of Governor-General. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Company administered its Indian territories through three Presidencies. These were Bengal, Madras and:
solution: The three PRESIDENCIES were BENGAL, MADRAS, and BOMBAY. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Assertion (A): Lord Cornwallis introduced administrative reforms in the Company's rule. Reason (R): He introduced the Permanent Settlement (1793) and reorganised the civil service and judiciary. Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: A is TRUE — Cornwallis introduced reforms. R is TRUE and EXPLAINS A: he introduced the PERMANENT SETTLEMENT (1793) and reorganised the CIVIL SERVICE and JUDICIARY. So option 1 is correct.

stem: British officials called 'Residents' posted in Indian states were essentially:
options: Political agents who interfered in the affairs of the state
solution: RESIDENTS were POLITICAL AGENTS placed in Indian states who INTERFERED in their AFFAIRS to serve Company interests. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The chief revenue and administrative officer of a district under Company rule was the:
solution: The COLLECTOR was the chief REVENUE and ADMINISTRATIVE officer of a DISTRICT under Company rule. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The word 'sepoy' is derived from the Persian/Urdu word 'sipahi', meaning:
solution: SEPOY comes from 'SIPAHI', meaning SOLDIER. So option 1 is correct.

stem: How many Anglo-Maratha Wars were fought before Maratha power was crushed?
solution: THREE Anglo-Maratha Wars were fought before Maratha power was finally broken (by 1818). So option 1 is correct.

stem: Maratha power was finally broken by the Company by around:
solution: MARATHA power was finally broken by the Company by around 1818 (Third Anglo-Maratha War). So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Company kept large standing armies in India mainly to:
options: Conquer and control territory and defend its interests
solution: The Company kept LARGE ARMIES to CONQUER and CONTROL territory and DEFEND its interests. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which battle-and-year pairing is correctly matched?
solution: Only 'BUXAR — 1764' is correct. Plassey was 1757; Wandiwash 1760. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The acquisition of Diwani rights in 1765 was economically significant because it allowed the Company to:
options: Use Bengal's revenue to finance trade and administration
solution: The DIWANI let the Company USE BENGAL's REVENUE to FINANCE its TRADE and ADMINISTRATION, a huge economic gain. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The devastating Bengal Famine of 1770, which killed millions, occurred under:
options: The Company's early revenue administration of Bengal
solution: The BENGAL FAMINE of 1770 occurred under the COMPANY's early REVENUE administration of Bengal, worsened by its policies. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Nawabs of Bengal in chronological order before Plassey included Murshid Quli Khan, Alivardi Khan and:
solution: The Nawabs before Plassey were Murshid Quli Khan, Alivardi Khan, and then SIRAJ-UD-DAULAH (defeated at Plassey). So option 1 is correct.

stem: Consider the following statements: 1. The Company gradually shifted from a trading body to a territorial power. 2. It used war, alliances and annexations to expand. Which is/are correct?
solution: BOTH are correct: the Company shifted from TRADE to TERRITORY (1), using WAR, ALLIANCES, and ANNEXATIONS to expand (2). So option 1 is correct.

stem: Robert Clive, who led the Company at Plassey, later became:
solution: ROBERT CLIVE, victor at Plassey, later became GOVERNOR of BENGAL. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Permanent Settlement of 1793 fixed the land revenue to be paid by the:
solution: The PERMANENT SETTLEMENT (1793) fixed the LAND REVENUE payable by the ZAMINDARS in Bengal. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Assertion (A): Tipu Sultan angered the Company. Reason (R): He stopped trade with the Company, modernised his army, and sought French support. Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: A is TRUE — Tipu angered the Company. R is TRUE and EXPLAINS A: he STOPPED TRADE with them, MODERNISED his ARMY, and sought FRENCH support. So option 1 is correct.

stem: By around 1857, the East India Company controlled:
options: Most of the Indian subcontinent, directly or through alliances
solution: By around 1857 the Company controlled MOST of the SUBCONTINENT, DIRECTLY or through ALLIANCES with princely states. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Company's claim that its authority was greater than that of Indian rulers reflected its ideology of:
solution: The Company's claim to supreme authority reflected the ideology of PARAMOUNTCY. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Which of the following best explains why the Nawabs of Bengal lost power to the Company?
options: Internal conflicts, financial dependence, betrayal by nobles, and Company military strength
They had no army at all
They gave up voluntarily out of friendship
solution: The Nawabs lost power due to INTERNAL CONFLICTS, FINANCIAL dependence, BETRAYAL by nobles (e.g., Mir Jafar), and Company MILITARY strength. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The Anglo-Maratha wars ended Maratha power, removing the last major Indian challenge to:
solution: The end of MARATHA power removed the last major Indian challenge to COMPANY SUPREMACY. So option 1 is correct.

stem: The overall theme of 'From Trade to Territory' is how the East India Company:
options: Transformed from a trading company into the ruler of a large Indian empire
solution: The theme is how the East India Company TRANSFORMED from a TRADING company into the RULER of a large Indian EMPIRE. So option 1 is correct.

stem: Among the European trading companies competing in India, the main rival the English defeated to establish their supremacy (notably in the Carnatic) were the:
solution: The English East India Company's chief European rival was the French; after the Carnatic Wars (English victory at Wandiwash, 1760) the French were reduced to a minor power, leaving the English supreme.
